name: Eligibility gate mixin
description: Methods on the autopilot run that decide, cheapest first, whether a run the backend scheduled goes ahead: the allowance for automatic extra runs (3 per autopilot a day and the team's budget; never a scheduled run and never Run now), backpressure per autopilot when the lane opts in, and unresolved HOLD decisions. WHEN a run is due is the backend's scheduler asking the hub's Proactivity, so nothing here reads a schedule.
advantages: Cheap, ordered and explainable gates that follow the person's settings exactly, and a scheduled run is never starved by a budget.
disadvantages: Only the runner can see extra runs and open work, so these stay here; a new setting needs a matching case.

name: Work sources
description: The registered kinds of work an autopilot can be tied to by its internal source slug (today learning, which asks the hub's Learning what reviews are due). A source run states its one scope, its bounds, its standing rules and what is due in the run's brief, and a source with nothing due refuses the run, which is closed as skipped with the reason and no model call.
advantages: A quiet week costs one bookkeeping row and no model call; a new kind of work is one registered object; the bounds are stated in the same brief as every other run.
disadvantages: Staying inside the source's scope is instructed in the brief, not enforced by tool permissions.

name: Goal routing by scope
description: Once per quest per day, a fast-tier judgment (the lane's model provider asked by tier, never a named model) gives each eligible goal (current period, incomplete, marked for AI help) to the ONE on-duty autopilot whose scope (its purpose and prompt) it fits best, or to none. A goal a rep holds stays with an on-duty autopilot of that rep with no judgment, a failed judgment leaves the goals alone, and words never decide, they only bound what the judge reads.
advantages: No goal is worked twice in a day and no autopilot is handed work outside its scope; the person never picks between goals and instructions.
disadvantages: A judgment costs one fast-tier call a day per quest, and a vague purpose and prompt route badly, so routing quality is a metric (metric-quest-autopilot-goal-routing).

name: Structure watch binding
description: Maps a quest's goals, experiments and investigations to the hub's structure digest and runs the hub's best-tier watch once per autopilot run of that quest, with the lane's own model provider asked by the call role's tier and its tokens and cost read per call. Every item is a decision request on the quest and no record is edited; no call is made when that quest's records did not change since its last watch, in a dry run, or when the lane switched it off (autopilot_structure_watch). Passed in by default by the poller. One real call over the hub's own records on 2026-11-10 on the best tier's default model: 1561 tokens in, 133 out, about 0.03 dollars on the keyless provider (its harness adds to the prompt's own tokens), no items; a lane with no model chosen for best fails with the reason.
advantages: Structure is looked at before more work is built on it, at the person's chosen autopilot frequency, for one small call a run; the hub keeps the logic, so a better arm there reaches every lane.
disadvantages: A quest's records are all a person's, so the watch can only propose; the first run on a quest has no earlier digest and always calls; a real run on a quest with items is not measured yet.

name: Quest AI latest look (no autopilot)
description: A standing per-quest schedule for the living Quest AI card, for every quest whether or not autopilot is on: the hub's Proactivity says it is due when the quest's own activity, a revisit date that has passed or a fully answered card came after the last look, Prioritization holds the activity trigger back for the minimum gap after the last look and orders what to look into (an overdue look again, a check on what the person did, the plan's open question). The host passes the signals and does the look; evaluated only when the person comes back.
advantages: A person who never turns autopilot on still sees Quest AI's recommendation change as their quest changes, at no cost for quests nobody opens; the timing and the order are the hub's, so a better arm there reaches it.
disadvantages: The host must read the quest's activity and pass it in; the gap and the kinds of work are Quest's policy held in this one module.
